name: Unity
version_context: UnityCsReference commit bf6028387a4fc2ea6d41aa7d8998e774655aedf6 (Unity 7000.0.0a12 C# reference source); Graphics tag v10.10.2, commit 0a547f7d17d69f0ea94f0f3143f8e5ea3b9f531f
summary: A proprietary game and real-time application engine. This card models the publicly released C# reference surface, Scriptable Render Pipeline sources, and official Unity 6 documentation; closed native engine internals are outside the evidence scope.

features.name: Scene and component lifecycle
features.description: The public C# reference exposes scene management and component-oriented runtime APIs, while the official manual describes MonoBehaviour event functions and scene execution. Unity therefore presents gameplay state through scenes, objects, and attached script components.
benefits: Provides an editor-visible composition model for runtime content
Allows reusable behavior to attach to scene objects through components
costs: Object and component lifecycle ordering must be understood across scene and play-mode transitions
The public API does not expose every native ownership and scheduling detail

features.name: Player loop and script execution stages
features.description: Unity exposes the PlayerLoop API and documents a staged execution order containing initialization, update, physics, animation, and rendering-related callbacks. The public API also permits replacing or customizing loop systems.
benefits: Makes major frame and simulation stages explicit to application code
Permits specialized systems to be inserted or removed from the loop
costs: Custom loop composition can invalidate assumptions made by packages and scripts
The exact order of callbacks and systems remains conditional on configuration and subsystem choices

features.name: Scriptable Render Pipeline boundary
features.description: The official Graphics repository contains the Scriptable Render Pipeline core and pipeline manager sources, while Unity documentation distinguishes built-in and Scriptable Render Pipeline execution. Rendering is therefore a replaceable package/pipeline boundary above engine scheduling and scene data.
benefits: Allows different rendering strategies to consume shared engine content
Provides package-level customization points for render passes and pipeline state
costs: Pipeline-specific behavior and package versions constrain portability
Rendering integration crosses public engine APIs and package implementation details

features.name: Editor, build, and runtime product boundary
features.description: The public reference separates Editor APIs and BuildPipeline bindings from Runtime and scene/player APIs. Together with the official build documentation, this supports a product boundary in which authoring/build tooling produces a runtime player artifact.
benefits: Separates authoring concerns from deployed player execution
Makes build configuration an explicit product-stage input
costs: Editor-only APIs and build-time transformations are not available in the player
A build can preserve or transform content in ways not visible from runtime APIs alone

features.name: Public reference-source boundary
features.description: Unity Technologies publishes UnityCsReference and the Graphics package sources, but the complete proprietary native engine is not represented by those repositories. This card consequently treats public bindings and packages as evidence for exposed contracts, not as a complete implementation claim.
benefits: Keeps product-level claims anchored to inspectable primary artifacts
Makes the boundary between documented contract and unobserved native implementation explicit
costs: Native scheduling, serialization, and renderer internals remain outside direct source evidence
Architecture conclusions must be narrower than claims about the whole commercial engine

mathematical_views.question: How does a frame transition through Unity's documented loop stages and configurable system groups?
assumptions: Loop systems are ordered stages with callbacks and subsystem work
Configuration can alter the set and position of systems
The model abstracts native scheduler implementation and platform-specific timing

mathematical_views.question: How do scenes, objects, components, and script lifecycle callbacks compose into runtime content state?
assumptions: Scene objects own or reference attached components
Component callbacks observe transitions in the player loop
The model abstracts serialization and native object ownership

mathematical_views.question: Which scene and frame state can be consumed by a selected render pipeline under its package contract?
assumptions: A pipeline is selected/configured above shared engine state
Pipeline packages expose distinct implementation and injection boundaries
Compatibility is a candidate relation and does not claim equal output across pipelines

mathematical_views.question: Which Unity product-stage claims are directly supported by public source and documentation, and which remain unobserved native implementation details?
assumptions: UnityCsReference and Graphics are authoritative for their published source scopes
Official manuals describe public behavior and contracts rather than all internals
Absence from the public repositories is not evidence that a native subsystem does not exist

benefits: Editor-authored content and reusable behavior share a compositional runtime model
costs: Lifecycle and ownership rules span scene, component, and native engine boundaries

benefits: Frame stages are inspectable and partially configurable
costs: Customization increases ordering and package-integration obligations

benefits: Rendering strategies can evolve as packages over shared content contracts
costs: Pipeline-specific semantics and versions limit complete interchangeability

benefits: Authoring and deployment concerns can be optimized independently
costs: Build transformations create a boundary between editor state and player state

benefits: Claims remain bounded by inspectable primary evidence
costs: The card cannot directly verify proprietary native implementation details
